summary:
The tree moved from b5c2b62 to a3d3860. That is a completed merge commit whose parents are 836e3a2 (SL-042's work) and 2e089a1 (uat with SL-040). There is no MERGE_HEAD, and no conflict markers remain in src/ or tests/. The builder's note that it did not commit is now moot, because the engine made the merge commit.

**What the merge changed on SL-042's side:**
- In ScanStore.cs, the class remarks keep SL-040's paragraph on raw sizes and then SL-042's paragraph on rollups. Size and OnDisk are now internal, as SL-040 made them.
- Every SL-042 line in ScanStore.cs, ScanStore.Rollup.cs and Scanner.cs is unchanged from what I reviewed at b5c2b62.
- The one semantic touchpoint the m8 note predicted was real. LargestFilesScaleTests built a 1 TB duplicate by passing EntryFlags.HardlinkDuplicate with ID 0, and the merged store clears that flag. It now appends the name as a later name of the file just before it. I checked that this is a real duplicate: entry i has i%1000==9 and repeats UInt128(1, i-1); entry i-1 has i%1000==8, is always a plain File with that ID, and sits in the same level2 folder. It is never a folder, a planted file or a link. So the store flags it and charges it nothing. If the ID failed to match, the test would fail, because a 1 TB name would top the list.
- LargestFiles reads only ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk of Files, so SL-042's change to folder charges does not affect it.
- The App calls LargestFiles.Top(result.Store) only after the scan returns. The SL-039 fitness rule permits exactly that.

**What I ran on the merged tree:**
- Forced rebuild (--no-incremental), Release: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The DLLs are newer than the sources.
- Full Core.Tests suite: 199 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- From the trx:
  - LargestFilesScaleTests passed: Top(100) over 4,417,469 entries in 23.8 ms, 26,400 bytes allocated.
  - The budget test retained 652.1 MiB, with a sampled peak of 678.4 MiB, against 800 MiB.
  - The timing test's 10 reads took 9.2–11.7 ms, against 250 ms.
  - TheAnalysisReadsOnlyChargedSizesAndOnlyFromTheStore passed.
- Fitness, after a rebuild: all 32 rules hold, including SL-040's analysis rule and SL-042's three.

**What the moved behaviour made false:** I looked for statements elsewhere in the repo that the changed behaviour has made untrue.
- docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 still says ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk return Size/OnDisk for every entry other than a Link or a HardlinkDuplicate. Since SL-042 they return 0 for every Folder. That file calls itself the authoritative as-built record. SL-042 made the line false at b5c2b62, and my first pass missed it. It is filed below as the only finding.
- The plants.json F17 note ("copied from Scanner.cs:267") now points at `private void Correct(...)`. The builder already raised this, so it is in drift.

I found no other stale statement in LargestFiles.cs, the LargestFilesTests comments, TopLevelTracker's remarks, the SL-039 doc or ScanResult's ScanTotals doc.

findings.claim: The project's as-built record of the byte-accessor contract is now false. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 says `ChargedSize(i)` and `ChargedOnDisk(i)` "return 0 for `Link` and for `HardlinkDuplicate` entries, and `Size`/`OnDisk` for every other entry". Since SL-042, ScanStore.Charges (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs:273-274) is true only for a File that is not a duplicate. A Folder, readable or Unreadable, now charges 0 whatever size it states. The same file opens by saying "Where this file and the original design disagree, this file is right. Do not 'correct' the code back". A later slice that reads SL-020's record will expect folder rows to charge their stated size. The tree slice is the likeliest, since this doc hands it the display accessor. It could put that behaviour back and double-count folders' own allocation in the rollups. Only docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md:15 states the new rule, and SL-020's record does not point to it.
findings.evidence: docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 against src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs:81-97 (the ChargedSize doc: "A folder (readable or not) and a link charge 0") and :273-274 (Charges). The project already keeps these records current when behaviour moves: SL-040 amended docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md with a 'Since SL-040' note in this same merge.
findings.fix: Amend docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 to read: 'return 0 for `Link`, for `HardlinkDuplicate` entries and, since SL-042, for every `Folder` whatever size it states; `Size`/`OnDisk` for a File that is charged (see docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md)'.

obligations.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ScanStoreRollupTests.cs AChainTenThousandFoldersDeepRollsEveryFileUpToEveryAncestor is unchanged by the merge and passed on a3d3860. Post is a loop (ScanStore.cs Post).
ScanStoreRollupTests.AFolderWithAHundredThousandChildrenRollsUpAcrossPageBoundaries is unchanged and passed on the merged tree.
All four rows of ScanStoreRollupTests.EmptyAndMixedTreesMatchTheOracleAtEveryCut passed on a3d3860.
ScanStoreRollupTests.OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFoldersIsChargedOnceToTheFirstNamesFolder passed on the merged tree.
ScanStoreRollupTests.NamesThatShareAnAncestorOrAParentChargeTheBytesOnceAndCountEveryName passed on the merged tree.
ScanStoreRollupTests.IdsThatMustNotMatchAreEachCharged passed. HasFileId in ScanStore.cs is unchanged by the merge.

ScanStoreRollupTests.ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing passed. It reads store.Size and store.OnDisk, which SL-040 made internal, through the test project's internals access and still compiles.

The synthetic ScanStoreRollupTests.AFolderThatStatesItsOwnSizeAddsNothingOfIt passed. The real-NTFS half was deferred under the m7 disposition, and I re-verified that reason in my first pass: FindFirstFileW lists a 1,500-file folder, and every folder in C:\Windows, System32 and C:\, at 0 bytes.
ScanStoreRollupTests.ChildrenAreReadLargestFirstWithEqualSizesInListingOrder passed. ScanStore.Rollup.cs is unchanged by the merge.
ScanStoreRollupTests.EachChildsShareIsItsOnDiskBytesOverTheFolders passed on the merged tree.
ScanStoreRollupTests.AFolderWithNothingOnDiskGivesEveryChildAZeroShare passed on the merged tree.

ScanStoreRollupTimingTests passed on a3d3860 in the full suite, with 10 reads of 9.2–11.7 ms against 250 ms. It shares the MemoryBudget collection with LargestFilesScaleTests, so it still runs without parallel contention.

Scans.AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals is unchanged. It also covers SL-040's real-tree LargestFilesTests, which go through Scans.Run: CheckStructure, root == Totals, and each TopLevelRow == its rollup. All 199 passed.
ScanStoreBudgetTests on the merged tree: retained 652.1 MiB, sampled peak 678.4 MiB, against 800 MiB (trx stdout).

Scanner.cs is unchanged by the merge. The probe trigger reads the firstHolder that Append returns (charged != entry), and CorrectSizes posts up the corrected row's chain. HardlinkTests (2,1) and (3,2) passed.
ScanStore.HasFileId is used by the private TryAddFileId and at the Scanner's three _settled sites. The merge left these unchanged.
The timing test is still in [Collection(nameof(MemoryBudget))]. The budget gate is still the GC-heap delta against 800 MiB. SL-040's LargestFilesScaleTests joined the same non-parallel collection.
ScanStore.Rollup.cs FilesBelow returns 1 for a File and 0 for a Link. CheckStructure passed on every real-tree scan on the merged tree.
Scanner.cs Credit(entry, posted, inPlace) is still the only writer of _files, _bytes and _bytesOnDisk.
ScanStoreRollupTests.AFolderListedInPartBeforeItsErrorKeepsWhatWasListed passed on a3d3860.

ScanStore.cs CheckParent is unchanged. ScanStoreRollupTests.AParentMustAlreadyBeInTheStoreAndOnlyTheRootHasNone passed. SL-040's scale test appends only under folders already in the store, so the check does not trip.
docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md still records the m7 probe output, which I reproduced independently in my first pass.

The merge note in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md was followed and gained an 'As merged' paragraph. The one duplicate built by hand, in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LargestFilesTests.cs:309-321, now comes from a repeated ID. A grep of tests/ finds no other Append that passes HardlinkDuplicate except the intentional ScanStoreRollupTests.cs:233, and no TryAddFileId.

docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md still carries the revised architecture line. The engine's own record is outside the worktree and waits on the open sort-on-read question, as the m9 disposition makes it conditional.

cases.evidence: ScanStoreRollupTests.AChainTenThousandFoldersDeepRollsEveryFileUpToEveryAncestor, unchanged by the merge. It builds a 10,000-folder chain with a file at every level and passed on a3d3860.
ScanStoreRollupTests.AFolderWithAHundredThousandChildrenRollsUpAcrossPageBoundaries: 100,000 children, 1,000 of them subfolders with 100 files each. Passed.
EmptyAndMixedTreesMatchTheOracleAtEveryCut: an empty root, nested empty folders, a 400-entry tree checked after every append, and a 50,000-entry mixed tree. Passed.
OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFoldersIsChargedOnceToTheFirstNamesFolder: one ID under three names in three folders, appended in a fixed order. Passed.
NamesThatShareAnAncestorOrAParentChargeTheBytesOnceAndCountEveryName covers a/x with a/b/y, and two names in one folder. Passed.
IdsThatMustNotMatchAreEachCharged: two files each with ID 0, all-ones and the widened 64-bit all-ones, plus a pair with the same low half and different high halves. Passed.
ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing: a link at 5000/8192 and an Unreadable folder at 4096/4096, and appends under the File, the Link and the Unreadable folder that must throw. Passed.

AFolderThatStatesItsOwnSizeAddsNothingOfIt feeds a synthetic 4096/4096 folder and passed. The real-NTFS half is not exercised, under the m7 deferral, and my earlier FindFirstFileW probe showed that reason holds.
ChildrenAreReadLargestFirstWithEqualSizesInListingOrder: 67 children with ties across files and folders, a duplicate last, read three times. Passed.
EachChildsShareIsItsOnDiskBytesOverTheFolders: shares of exactly 3/4 and 1/4, 1/3 within 1e-12, and shares summing to 1. Passed.
AFolderWithNothingOnDiskGivesEveryChildAZeroShare: an empty folder, a folder of only duplicates, and online-only files; a File, a Link and an Unreadable folder return []. Passed.

ScanStoreRollupTimingTests on the merged tree, in the full suite: 10 reads of 9.2–11.7 ms. The first read is JIT-cold only when the test runs alone, which I measured at 37 ms on the unchanged ChildrenLargestFirst.
Scans.AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals runs on every real-tree scan, SL-040's LargestFilesTests included. HardlinkTests puts the stale first name first. All 199 passed on a3d3860.
ScanStoreBudgetTests: 5M entries with the three columns on every row and one 100,000-child folder. Retained 652.1 MiB, sampled peak 678.4 MiB, against 800 MiB.

drift: No undeclared code departure. The merge kept SL-040's internal Size/OnDisk and all of SL-042's code as it was. The one semantic touchpoint, the hand-built duplicate in LargestFilesScaleTests, is fixed and recorded in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md under 'As merged'.

eng/rules-harness/plants.json row F17 says its planted text was 'copied from Scanner.cs:267'. SL-042 deleted that line, and Scanner.cs:267 is now `private void Correct(...)`. The plant still anchors on 'int entries = store.Count;' in LargestFiles.cs, which exists, so the harness is unaffected. The builder raised it as a follow-up.
The builder's declared departure, that it did not commit and left MERGE_HEAD set, is moot. The engine committed a3d3860 with parents 836e3a2 and 2e089a1, and no merge is in progress.

Carried from attempt 1: the m9 revision (children ordered largest first on read, none stored) exists only in docs/design/SL-042-folder-totals.md. The engine's own architecture record still says children are stored sorted.
unreviewed: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml, src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs, tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs, tests/window/WindowCases.ps1, tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1: these came in with SL-040 from uat and have already been reviewed on that slice. I checked only whether they read the store or totals in a way SL-042 changed. The App reads result.Store only after the scan returns, through LargestFiles.Top and GetPath, and WindowCases compares report topLevel against core totals. Beyond that I did not review their layout or harness logic.
